title: Holographic Local Operator Quenches with Conserved Momentum and Spin
authors: Pawel Caputa, Pedro Castellini Grand, Justin R. David, Rahul Metya
abstract: We investigate the holographic dictionary relating point particles carrying longitudinal momentum or angular momentum in asymptotically AdS$_3$ spacetimes to suitably regulated, time-evolved states created by local primary operators in the dual two-dimensional conformal field theory (2D CFT). We find that asymmetric left/right Euclidean smearing of local operators produces states carrying momentum, and the corresponding bulk excitation is a particle with conserved momentum. We compute the energy density and entanglement entropy in these states and in their dual back-reacted geometries, finding exact agreement between the CFT and gravity descriptions. We further extend this correspondence to particles with intrinsic spin, whose CFT duals are primary operators with unequal holomorphic and anti-holomorphic scaling dimensions. We again find a precise match between CFT and holographic calculations of energy densities and entanglement entropies. Finally, we explore applications of these setups beyond holography by deriving the evolution of Rényi entropies in 2D rational CFTs and introducing a new class of local quantum quench protocols with conserved longitudinal or angular momentum.
summary: This work extends the holographic dictionary to include point particles carrying conserved momentum and spin in AdS_3. By calculating observables like energy density and entanglement entropy on both the gravity and CFT sides, the authors demonstrate precise quantitative agreement. This establishes a robust framework for studying non-equilibrium dynamics in strongly coupled systems using conserved charges.
main_problem: The paper investigates the holographic dictionary connecting point particles with conserved momentum or spin in AdS_3 spacetime to time-evolved states created by local primary operators in the dual 2D CFT.
main_result: The authors find exact agreement between CFT and gravity descriptions for energy density and entanglement entropy when considering conserved momentum and intrinsic spin in these holographic quenches.
method: The study employs the AdS/CFT correspondence, calculating back-reacted geometries and stress tensors on the gravity side, and comparing these results with calculations of entanglement entropy and energy density on the CFT side.
model_or_system: The system involves massive particles propagating in asymptotically AdS_3 spacetimes (Poincaré, Global, BTZ) on the gravity side, dual to local primary operators in a 2D CFT on the field theory side.
key_observables: Energy density, entanglement entropy (and Rényi entropies), and the stress tensor components.
important_parameters: Longitudinal momentum, angular momentum, intrinsic spin, and the AdS radius (R).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies fundamentally on the AdS/CFT correspondence and extends previous work to include conserved charges beyond simple energy quenches.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the particle's trajectory in Poincaré coordinates, while Figure 2 shows the time evolution of energy and momentum density derived from the stress tensor.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the gravity setup for charged particles, detailing the CFT description via local operator quenches, calculating entanglement entropy in AdS_3/CFT_2, extending the analysis to include intrinsic spin, and concluding with applications to rational CFTs and general local quenches.
why_interesting: The rigorous matching of conserved charges (momentum/spin) between gravity and CFT provides powerful, concrete examples of how quantum information measures behave in non-equilibrium, strongly coupled systems, relevant to understanding quantum chaos.
